name: str_pad
title: Pad a string to minimum width

origin.description: Pad each string out to a minimum width. A longer string is returned unchanged.
origin.usage: str_pad(string, width, side = c("left", "right", "both"), pad = " ", use_width = TRUE)

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Minimum width of the padded strings.

arguments.name: side
arguments.text: Where to add the pad: "left" (the default), "right", or "both". The whole word is required.

arguments.name: pad
arguments.text: A single padding character. The default is a space.

arguments.name: use_width
arguments.text: If true, measure display width. If false, measure the number of code points.

origin.details: string, width, and pad share one size: a length-1 vector recycles, and two other lengths must agree. An odd both-sides gap puts the extra pad on the right. use_width false counts code points, so a wide character takes one column.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as the common size of string, width, and pad.
origin.example:
print(rbind(
  str_pad("hadley", 30, "left"),
  str_pad("hadley", 30, "right"),
  str_pad("hadley", 30, "both")
))
print(str_pad(c("a", "abc", "abcdef"), 10))
print(str_pad("a", c(5, 10, 20)))
print(str_pad("a", 10, pad = c("-", "_", " ")))
print(str_pad("hadley", 3))

translation.description: Pad each string out to a minimum width. A longer string is returned unchanged. The result is a list. A missing string is stringi._na.NA.

translation.details: string, width, and pad share one size: a length-1 vector recycles, and two other lengths must agree. An odd both-sides gap puts the extra pad on the right. use_width false counts code points, so a wide character takes one column. The Python result is a list, and a missing string is stringi._na.NA.
translation.value: A character vector the same length as the common size of string, width, and pad.
translation.example:
from stringr.pad import str_pad
print([
    str_pad("hadley", 30, "left"),
    str_pad("hadley", 30, "right"),
    str_pad("hadley", 30, "both"),
])
print(str_pad(["a", "abc", "abcdef"], 10))
print(str_pad("a", [5, 10, 20]))
print(str_pad("a", 10, pad=["-", "_", " "]))
print(str_pad("hadley", 3))
